note: Single source of truth for every tool ChainCodeCamp teaches. Read by the Setup Hub, the quick-install drawers and the setup score. Windows steps assume WSL for anything that touches the EVM toolchain.

tools.name: VS Code
tools.what: The editor you will live in. Solidity syntax highlighting, Foundry test runs, and the Aderyn and Certora extensions all plug into it.
tools.why: You read more code than you write as an auditor. You need fast search across a cloned repo and a terminal one keystroke away.

steps: PowerShell: winget install Microsoft.VisualStudioCode
Open VS Code, press Ctrl+Shift+X, install the extensions: Solidity, Solidity Visual Developer, GitLens
Press Ctrl+` to open the integrated terminal. This is where you will run forge.
brew install --cask visual-studio-code
Or download the .dmg from the official link
Install the Solidity and GitLens extensions from the Extensions panel.
Ubuntu/Debian: download the .deb from the official link, then sudo apt install ./code_*.deb
Or add the Microsoft apt repo as shown on https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/linux
Install the Solidity and GitLens extensions.

stuck.problem: 'code' is not recognized as a command (Windows).
stuck.fix: In VS Code press Ctrl+Shift+P and run "Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH", then reopen the terminal. Mac has the same entry in the Command Palette.

stuck.problem: Extensions installed on Windows do not show up inside WSL.
stuck.fix: Extensions are per-environment. Open the folder inside WSL, then click 'Install in WSL: Ubuntu' on the Solidity extension page.

stuck.problem: Solidity files have no syntax highlighting.
stuck.fix: Install the extension named Solidity by Juan Blanco (or Solidity Visual Developer), reload the window, and make sure the .sol file is inside the folder you opened.

tools.name: Git
tools.what: Version control. Every CCC challenge ends with a commit you push to GitHub, and every practice repo is a git clone.
tools.why: Auditors prove their work with git history: the PoC test, the fix, the report. It is also the only sane way to pull updates from the practice repos.

steps: PowerShell: winget install Git.Git
Close and reopen the terminal so PATH updates, then set your identity once:
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
xcode-select --install (installs git from Apple)
Or: brew install git
git config --global user.name "Your Name" and git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y git
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"

stuck.problem: push to GitHub fails with 'Authentication failed'.
stuck.fix: Use Git Credential Manager (the Windows installer default) and sign in when it prompts, or create a Personal Access Token on GitHub > Settings > Developer settings and use it as the password.

stuck.problem: warning: LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it.
stuck.fix: Harmless on Windows. If it annoys you: git config --global core.autocrlf input

stuck.problem: 'git' is not recognized after installing.
stuck.fix: Your terminal opened before the installer finished PATH changes. Close every terminal window, open a new one, confirm with git --version before anything else.

tools.name: Node.js
tools.what: JavaScript runtime and package manager (npm). Needed for Hardhat, the Tenderly CLI, the Aderyn npm build, and for running ChainCodeCamp locally.
tools.why: Half the tooling in this course ships on npm. Node 18.17+ is the floor for modern Hardhat and for this site's dev server.

steps: PowerShell: winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS
Reopen the terminal.
Optional: npm install -g npm@latest to update npm itself.
brew install node
Or download the LTS installer from the official link
Verify both node and npm before continuing.
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.40.1/install.sh | bash
source ~/.bashrc
nvm install --lts
Never use sudo npm install -g. nvm owns your global packages.

stuck.problem: npm ERR! unsupported engine, or syntax errors on a fresh clone.
stuck.fix: Your Node is too old. node -v must be 18.17 or higher. On Windows: winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS, then reopen the terminal.

stuck.problem: EACCES permission denied installing a global package (Mac/Linux).
stuck.fix: Never use sudo npm. Use nvm (Linux steps above) or brew so your user owns the global prefix.

stuck.problem: npm install hangs or times out on a slow connection.
stuck.fix: Run npm install --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund. Those flags skip audit calls that stall on weak networks.

tools.name: WSL
tools.what: Windows Subsystem for Linux: a real Ubuntu shell inside Windows. It is how almost every Ethereum security tool expects to run on a PC.
tools.why: Slither, Echidna, Medusa, Aderyn, Foundry and every audit repo in this course are built and tested on Linux first. On Windows you use WSL and skip an entire class of install errors.

steps: Open PowerShell as Administrator and run: wsl --install
Restart the PC when asked, open 'Ubuntu' from the Start menu, create your Linux user.
Inside Ubuntu: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential curl git
Run the rest of this setup hub inside the Ubuntu terminal, not PowerShell.
Not needed on Mac. Mark it installed with the reason 'not applicable on this OS'.
Not needed on Linux. Mark it installed with the reason 'not applicable on this OS'.

stuck.problem: 'wsl --install' says the virtual machine platform is not enabled.
stuck.fix: Control Panel > Turn Windows features on or off > check 'Virtual Machine Platform' and 'Windows Subsystem for Linux', reboot, then run wsl --install again.

stuck.problem: WSL 1 got installed instead of WSL 2.
stuck.fix: Run wsl --set-default-version 2 and wsl --update. For an existing distro: wsl --set-version Ubuntu 2

stuck.problem: The Ubuntu window closes immediately on first launch.
stuck.fix: Run wsl --update in PowerShell, then relaunch Ubuntu. If it still dies, wsl --unregister Ubuntu then wsl --install -d Ubuntu (this wipes that distro, only safe on a fresh install).

tools.name: Foundry
tools.what: The Ethereum development toolkit written in Rust: forge (build and test), cast (talk to chains from the terminal), anvil (a local chain), chisel (a Solidity REPL).
tools.why: Every CCC lesson runs forge. You compile, fuzz, invariant-test and deploy with it, and you write your exploit proofs as forge tests.

steps: Inside WSL (Ubuntu): curl -L https://getfoundry.sh/install | bash && foundryup
Close and reopen the Ubuntu terminal.
PowerShell also works (Invoke-RestMethod https://getfoundry.paradigm.xyz | Invoke-Expression) but WSL is what this course uses.
In any project: forge install foundry-rs/forge-std
curl -L https://getfoundry.sh/install | bash && foundryup
Reopen the terminal.
Apple Silicon runs the arm64 binary natively, nothing extra to do.
curl -L https://getfoundry.sh/install | bash && foundryup
Reopen the terminal, then confirm all four binaries:
forge --version && cast --version && anvil --version && chisel --version

stuck.problem: foundryup: command not found after install.
stuck.fix: The installer appended to your shell profile. Run source ~/.bashrc (or open a new terminal) then foundryup again. On Windows do it inside WSL, not PowerShell.

stuck.problem: forge build fails with 'does not exist: lib/forge-std'.
stuck.fix: Dependencies are not installed: run forge install foundry-rs/forge-std in the project root, or git submodule update --init --recursive on a cloned audit repo.

stuck.problem: forge test hangs downloading solc, or fails with no internet.
stuck.fix: Foundry downloads each solc version on first use. Run it once with connectivity or pre-install with svm install <version>. Check the pinned solc version in foundry.toml first.

tools.name: Python
tools.what: Python 3.10+. Several analyzers (Slither, Halmos, the Certora CLI) are Python programs, and pip is how they get installed.
tools.why: You need a working python3 before any analysis tool will install. On Windows, install it inside WSL and leave PowerShell alone.

steps: Inside WSL (Ubuntu): sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-pip python3-venv
Native alternative: winget install Python.Python.3.12 (check 'Add python.exe to PATH').
The course assumes python3 inside WSL.
brew install python
Or download the installer from the official link.
macOS ships python3 already; brew guarantees a current version.
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-pip python3-venv
Ubuntu 22.04 ships 3.10, the minimum for every tool here.

stuck.problem: On Windows, 'python' opens the Microsoft Store instead of a shell.
stuck.fix: Settings > Apps > Advanced app settings > App execution aliases, turn off both python.exe aliases, then reinstall with winget or just use python3 inside WSL.

stuck.problem: error: externally-managed-environment when you pip install.
stuck.fix: Modern Linux blocks system-wide pip. Use pipx for tools (next card) or a venv: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate

stuck.problem: python3 --version prints 3.6 or 3.8 on an old distro.
stuck.fix: Tools need 3.10+. On Ubuntu use the deadsnakes PPA: sudo add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa && sudo apt update && sudo apt install python3.12, or upgrade the distro.

tools.name: pipx
tools.what: Installs Python command line tools into their own isolated environment so they never fight with your system Python.
tools.why: It is the clean way to get Slither, Halmos and the Certora CLI without breaking anything else on the machine.

steps: Inside WSL (Ubuntu): sudo apt install -y pipx && pipx ensurepath
Reopen the terminal so PATH updates.
Native alternative: python -m pip install --user pipx && python -m pipx ensurepath
brew install pipx
pipx ensurepath
Reopen the terminal.
sudo apt install -y pipx && pipx ensurepath
Or: python3 -m pip install --user pipx && python3 -m pipx ensurepath
Reopen the terminal so ~/.local/bin lands on PATH.

stuck.problem: pipx: command not found after install.
stuck.fix: Run pipx ensurepath, then open a new terminal (or source ~/.bashrc). On Ubuntu, ~/.local/bin must be on PATH.

stuck.problem: pipx says a package is installed but its command is missing.
stuck.fix: pipx reinstall-all, then pipx list to see which binaries exist.

stuck.problem: apt says pipx has no installation candidate.
stuck.fix: Old Ubuntu. Fall back to: python3 -m pip install --user pipx && python3 -m pipx ensurepath

tools.name: Slither
tools.what: Trail of Bits' static analyzer for Solidity. It reads the compiler's AST and flags reentrancy, unchecked calls, shadowing, bad comparisons and dozens of other issue classes.
tools.why: It is the first pass on every audit: run it in minute one, triage the output, then read the code the report points at.

steps: Inside WSL with python3 and pipx ready: pipx install slither-analyzer
Foundry must be installed too, Slither shells out to forge build.
cd into a Foundry project before running it.
pipx install slither-analyzer
First run downloads the pinned solc for the project, so stay online once.
brew install git is a prerequisite for repo-wide analysis.
pipx install slither-analyzer
cd into a Foundry project, then run: slither .
First run downloads the pinned solc for that project.

stuck.problem: solc errors, or 'No solc version set'.
stuck.fix: Run inside a project that pins solc (foundry.toml or hardhat config). For bare files: pipx install solc-select && solc-select install 0.8.20 && solc-select use 0.8.20, then slither . --solc solc-0.8.20

stuck.problem: Slither cannot find forge or hardhat in the project.
stuck.fix: Slither uses the framework build. Run forge build first in a Foundry repo (npm install for Hardhat) and always run Slither from the project root.

stuck.problem: On Windows native, crytic-compile fails with Python or path errors.
stuck.fix: Use WSL. Everything in this course runs from the Ubuntu shell where paths and line endings behave.

tools.name: Aderyn
tools.what: Cyfrin's Rust-based static analyzer. It is faster than Slither on big repos, needs no solc environment, and writes a Markdown report you can paste into an audit submission.
tools.why: Second opinion. Slither and Aderyn find different things, and running both is standard on competitive audits.

steps: Inside WSL: curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cyfrin/up/main/install | bash, then run: cyfrinup
Alternative without cyfrinup: npm install @cyfrin/aderyn -g
Windows users must have WSL installed first.
brew install cyfrin/tap/aderyn
Or: curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/cyfrin/aderyn/releases/latest/download/aderyn-installer.sh | bash
Upgrade later by re-running the installer or cyfrinup.
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/cyfrin/aderyn/releases/latest/download/aderyn-installer.sh | bash
Or install cyfrinup and run cyfrinup.
Or: npm install @cyfrin/aderyn -g

stuck.problem: Old aderyn version keeps reporting the same stale findings.
stuck.fix: If you installed via the curl installer, run aderyn-update. Via cyfrinup, re-run cyfrinup. Via npm, npm install @cyfrin/aderyn -g again.

stuck.problem: A very old aderyn sits in ~/.cyfrin/bin and shadows the new one.
stuck.fix: Remove it: rm -f ~/.cyfrin/bin/aderyn, then which aderyn to confirm the path points at the npm or brew install.

stuck.problem: aderyn: command not found on Windows PowerShell.
stuck.fix: Aderyn expects WSL on Windows. Run it from the Ubuntu shell, not PowerShell.

tools.name: Echidna
tools.what: Crytic's Haskell property fuzzer. It generates thousands of random call sequences against your contract and looks for the one that breaks your assertion.
tools.why: Unit tests prove one path. Echidna proves the property holds across every path you did not think of.

steps: Inside WSL (Ubuntu), download the latest Linux binary from the GitHub releases page, then: chmod +x echidna && sudo mv echidna /usr/local/bin/
Alternative: docker run -v $PWD:/workdir ghcr.io/crytic/echidna/echidna:latest (needs Docker Desktop with WSL backend)
There is no native Windows build, WSL is the supported path.
brew install echidna
Or download the macOS binary from the GitHub releases page.
On Apple Silicon, check the release notes for a native arm64 build before using the binary.
Download the Linux binary from the GitHub releases page, then chmod +x echidna and move it onto PATH.
Or: docker run -v $PWD:/workdir ghcr.io/crytic/echidna/echidna:latest
Or build from source with stack (Haskell toolchain required).

stuck.problem: echidna: command not found after downloading the binary.
stuck.fix: You skipped chmod and PATH: chmod +x echidna && sudo mv echidna /usr/local/bin/. Confirm with which echidna.

stuck.problem: 'Permission denied' when running the binary.
stuck.fix: The executable bit was lost in transfer (common after downloading on Windows then copying to WSL). Re-run chmod +x, and make sure the binary is the Linux build.

stuck.problem: Fuzzer runs but never finds your bug.
stuck.fix: Check your contract actually deploys in the fuzzer (compile errors print first), give it a high enough gas and depth budget in echidna.yaml, and seed state in the test contract. Long reentrancy chains need depth, not luck.

tools.name: Medusa
tools.what: Crytic's newer fuzzer, written on top of go-ethereum. Parallel workers, coverage-guided mutation, and a corpus that keeps any call sequence that reaches new code.
tools.why: Same job as Echidna, different search strategy. When a property survives one fuzzer, running the second is cheap insurance.

steps: Inside WSL: install Go first (sudo apt install -y golang-go), then: go install github.com/crytic/medusa@latest
Binaries for Windows and Linux are also published on the releases page.
Make sure $(go env GOPATH)/bin is on PATH.
brew install go, then: go install github.com/crytic/medusa@latest
Or download the macOS binary from the releases page.
export PATH="$PATH:$(go env GOPATH)/bin" if medusa is not found.
sudo apt install -y golang-go (any recent Go works)
go install github.com/crytic/medusa@latest
export PATH="$PATH:$(go env GOPATH)/bin"

stuck.problem: medusa: command not found after go install.
stuck.fix: GOPATH/bin is not on PATH. Run export PATH="$PATH:$(go env GOPATH)/bin" (add it to ~/.bashrc) and confirm with which medusa.

stuck.problem: go install fails with 'go: module not found' or proxy timeouts.
stuck.fix: Check connectivity and proxy: GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct go install github.com/crytic/medusa@latest, or grab the release binary instead.

stuck.problem: Medusa cannot compile the project.
stuck.fix: It reuses your Foundry build. Run forge build in the repo first, and run medusa from the project root where foundry.toml lives.

tools.name: Halmos
tools.what: Symbolic testing for Solidity by a16z. Instead of random inputs it asks a solver to find an input that falsifies your assertion, so it checks all inputs at once for bounded code.
tools.why: Fuzzing samples. Halmos proves for the paths it can bound, and it runs on your existing Foundry test names without new syntax.

steps: Inside WSL: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh, then: uv tool install --python 3.12 halmos
Docker alternative: docker pull ghcr.io/a16z/halmos:latest (includes Python, solvers and Foundry)
pip path (advanced): python3.12 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install halmos
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
uv tool install --python 3.12 halmos
Update later with: uv tool upgrade halmos
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
uv tool install --python 3.12 halmos
Or: docker pull ghcr.io/a16z/halmos:latest

stuck.problem: halmos: command not found after uv tool install.
stuck.fix: uv puts tools in ~/.local/bin. Run the PATH line the installer printed (or source ~/.bashrc), open a new terminal, and confirm with which halmos.

stuck.problem: pip install halmos refuses (externally-managed-environment) or picks the wrong Python.
stuck.fix: uv handles the Python version for you (that is why it is recommended). If you insist on pip, use a python3.12 venv first.

stuck.problem: Halmos times out or returns unknown on a function.
stuck.fix: Symbolic execution explodes with unbounded loops and dynamic arrays. Bound the loop (add --loop), narrow the assertion, or use fuzzing for that part instead.

tools.name: Certora
tools.what: Commercial formal verification. You write rules in CVL (Certora Verification Language) and the Prover checks them against every possible state, not sampled ones.
tools.why: Intro level: you will read and run one example to know what a machine-checked proof looks like and when a property deserves one. Teams like Aave and MakerDAO use it on core invariants.

steps: Inside WSL: python3 -m pip install certora-cli (or pipx install certora-cli)
Prerequisites: Python 3.9+ and JDK 21+ (sudo apt install -y openjdk-21-jdk)
Register on certora.com for a free personal access key, then export CERTORAKEY=<your key>
windows.expected: usage: certoraRun ... (prints the CLI usage block)

steps: python3 -m pip install certora-cli (or pipx install certora-cli)
Prerequisites: Python 3.9+ and JDK 21+ (brew install openjdk@21)
export CERTORAKEY=<your key> after registering on certora.com
mac.expected: usage: certoraRun ... (prints the CLI usage block)

steps: python3 -m pip install certora-cli (or pipx install certora-cli)
Prerequisites: Python 3.9+ and JDK 21+ (sudo apt install -y openjdk-21-jdk)
export CERTORAKEY=<your key> after registering on certora.com
linux.expected: usage: certoraRun ... (prints the CLI usage block)

stuck.problem: certoraRun: command not found.
stuck.fix: pip installed it outside PATH. Add the path pip printed (Linux: ~/.local/bin) to PATH in ~/.profile, or install with pipx and run pipx ensurepath.

stuck.problem: 'CERTORAKEY is not set' or authentication failed.
stuck.fix: Create the key on the Certora site after registering, then export CERTORAKEY=<key> in the shell (put it in ~/.bashrc to keep it). Never commit the key to git.

stuck.problem: Java version errors.
stuck.fix: The Prover needs JDK 21+. Check java --version; install with sudo apt install -y openjdk-21-jdk (Linux) or brew install openjdk@21 (Mac).

tools.name: Tenderly
tools.what: A transaction debugger and simulation platform. Paste a hash and see every execution step, storage change and revert reason, then fork mainnet state and try your exploit before it costs real money.
tools.why: When your PoC passes on anvil but you need to explain a real mainnet hack or debug a failing fork test, Tenderly is the microscope.

steps: Web app first: create an account at tenderly.co, no install needed for debugging.
CLI (inside WSL): npm install -g @tenderly/tenderly-cli
Sign in: tenderly login
Create an account at tenderly.co for the web debugger.
CLI: npm install -g @tenderly/tenderly-cli
tenderly login
Create an account at tenderly.co for the web debugger.
CLI: npm install -g @tenderly/tenderly-cli
tenderly login

stuck.problem: tenderly: command not found after npm install -g.
stuck.fix: Your npm global bin folder is not on PATH. npm config get prefix shows it; add its bin folder to PATH, reopen the terminal, never use sudo npm.

stuck.problem: Login opens a browser you cannot reach (headless server or WSL).
stuck.fix: tenderly login prints a URL: open it on your phone or host machine, then paste the code back into the terminal.

stuck.problem: Simulation says the project or access token is missing.
stuck.fix: Run tenderly login again, or set TENDERLY_ACCESS_KEY from your Tenderly account settings and export it in the shell.

tools.name: Etherscan
tools.what: The Ethereum block explorer. Source-verified contract code, transaction traces, internal calls, token transfers and event logs for every mainnet contract.
tools.why: Recon starts here: read the deployed source of the protocol you are auditing, check who called the admin function, and pull the exact transaction of a historic hack.

steps: No install: bookmark https://etherscan.io/
For scripts: create a free account, open https://etherscan.io/myapikey, copy an API key.
Store the key in an environment variable, never in git.
windows.expected: Your API key list page loads (empty until you create one)

steps: No install: bookmark https://etherscan.io/
For scripts: create a free account and copy an API key from the MyAPIKey page.
Store the key in an environment variable, never in git.
mac.expected: Your API key list page loads

steps: No install: bookmark https://etherscan.io/
For scripts: create a free account and copy an API key from the MyAPIKey page.
Store the key in an environment variable, never in git.
linux.expected: Your API key list page loads

stuck.problem: 'This contract is not verified' on the address you are auditing.
stuck.fix: Check the explorer for that chain (basescan.org, arbiscan.com, polygonscan.com), find the verified proxy implementation under the Contract tab, or ask the team for the commit hash.

stuck.problem: API returns 'Missing/Invalid API Key' or rate limit errors.
stuck.fix: Free tier allows 5 requests per second. Pass the key as &apikey=, keep it out of git, and sleep between loop requests.

stuck.problem: The transaction you need is not on mainnet.
stuck.fix: Switch to the right explorer for that chain, or use etherscan.io/tx/<hash> only for Ethereum mainnet hashes.

tools.name: Remix
tools.what: The browser Solidity IDE at remix.ethereum.org. Compiler, deploy buttons, a storage inspector and plugins, all in a tab.
tools.why: Fastest way to demo a bug: paste a contract, deploy to the Remix VM, click, watch the exploit happen, no toolchain needed.

steps: No install: open https://remix.ethereum.org/ in your browser.
Optional: install MetaMask and connect it to a testnet for real transactions.
Optional local bridge for big repos: npm install -g @remix-project/remixd
windows.expected: The Remix IDE loads with the file explorer on the left

steps: No install: open https://remix.ethereum.org/ in your browser.
Optional: install MetaMask and connect it to a testnet.
Optional local bridge: npm install -g @remix-project/remixd
mac.expected: The Remix IDE loads with the file explorer on the left

steps: No install: open https://remix.ethereum.org/ in your browser.
Optional: install MetaMask and connect it to a testnet.
Optional local bridge: npm install -g @remix-project/remixd
linux.expected: The Remix IDE loads with the file explorer on the left

stuck.problem: Files you edited locally do not appear in Remix.
stuck.fix: Remix stores files in browser storage. Run remixd in the project root and connect it from the RemixDEPLOY (File Providers) plugin to bridge the local folder.

stuck.problem: Compiler fails to load a solc version.
stuck.fix: In the Solidity compiler panel pick the version from the dropdown. If the download stalls on a blocked network, fall back to the local toolchain (forge build).

stuck.problem: Injected provider (MetaMask) does not connect.
stuck.fix: MetaMask must be unlocked and on the network Remix expects. Start with the Remix VM or a testnet, never with your main wallet on mainnet.

tools.name: Hardhat
tools.what: The JavaScript smart contract development environment: compile, test in TypeScript, deploy scripts, and a mainnet forking debugger.
tools.why: Many real audit targets are Hardhat repos, not Foundry repos. You need both so no codebase is closed to you.

steps: Inside WSL, in an empty folder: npm init -y
npm install --save-dev hardhat
npx hardhat init and pick the sample project
In an empty folder: npm init -y
npm install --save-dev hardhat
npx hardhat init and pick the sample project
In an empty folder: npm init -y
npm install --save-dev hardhat
npx hardhat init and pick the sample project

stuck.problem: npx hardhat init fails or prints engine errors.
stuck.fix: Node is too old: node -v must be 18.17+. Reinstall the LTS (see the Node card) and delete node_modules plus package-lock.json before retrying.

stuck.problem: Tests pass locally but fail with 'Invalid account' or nonce errors.
stuck.fix: Your hardhat.config network accounts or RPC URL is wrong. Never commit private keys; use a .env file that is git-ignored, or anvil for local work.

stuck.problem: Forking mainnet hangs or times out.
stuck.fix: Free RPC endpoints are rate limited. Use a dedicated provider key (Alchemy, Infura, or a public archive endpoint) in hardhat.config networks.

tools.name: MetaMask
tools.what: The browser wallet. It holds keys, signs transactions, and exposes an injected provider that web3 apps (Remix, Tenderly, testnet faucets) talk to.
tools.why: You need a wallet to deploy to a testnet, claim faucet ETH, and watch a transaction land on chain. Use a throwaway account for learning, never your funds wallet.

steps: Install the browser extension for Chrome, Firefox, Brave or Edge from the official download page (verify the domain, wallet drainers clone this page).
Create a wallet, write the seed phrase on paper, and never paste it into any website.
Add a testnet: the wallet's network picker has Sepolia built in.
windows.verify: check the extension icon shows your account and the network bar says Sepolia
windows.expected: A 0x address is visible and the network reads Sepolia

steps: Install the browser extension from the official download page.
Create a wallet, write the seed phrase on paper, never paste it into any website.
Switch the network bar to Sepolia for testnet work.
mac.verify: check the extension icon shows your account and the network bar says Sepolia
mac.expected: A 0x address is visible and the network reads Sepolia

steps: Install the browser extension from the official download page.
Create a wallet, write the seed phrase on paper, never paste it into any website.
Switch the network bar to Sepolia for testnet work.
linux.verify: check the extension icon shows your account and the network bar says Sepolia
linux.expected: A 0x address is visible and the network reads Sepolia

stuck.problem: 'MetaMask provider is not connected' inside Remix.
stuck.fix: Unlock MetaMask, approve the site connection when prompted, and make sure the selected network matches what the page expects (start on Sepolia or the Remix VM).

stuck.problem: Transactions fail with 'insufficient funds for gas'.
stuck.fix: Testnet ETH is free. Use a Sepolia faucet (the network picker links one) and wait for it to arrive. Mainnet ETH costs real money, do not practice there.

stuck.problem: Wrong account or wrong network keeps being used.
stuck.fix: Click the account icon to switch accounts and the network bar to switch networks. Both selections are per-site, so check them whenever a dapp misbehaves.

tools.name: GitHub
tools.what: Where your work is proven. CCC pushes practice repos, PoC tests, audit reports and the final portfolio here.
tools.why: Competitive audit platforms and employers judge you by the repo. A green commit history of PoCs beats any certificate.

steps: Create an account at https://github.com/
Install the CLI (optional but used by the push check): winget install GitHub.cli
gh auth login and follow the browser flow.
git is required first, see the Git card.
windows.expected: Logged in to github.com account <your handle>

steps: Create an account at https://github.com/
CLI (optional): brew install gh
gh auth login and follow the browser flow.
mac.expected: Logged in to github.com account <your handle>

steps: Create an account at https://github.com/
CLI (optional): sudo apt install -y gh (or the official apt repo for older distros)
gh auth login and follow the browser flow.
linux.expected: Logged in to github.com account <your handle>

stuck.problem: git push asks for a username and password and then rejects it.
stuck.fix: GitHub no longer accepts account passwords. Use Git Credential Manager's sign-in window, or generate a Personal Access Token (Settings > Developer settings > Tokens) and use it as the password.

stuck.problem: gh auth login fails with 'gh: command not found'.
stuck.fix: The CLI is optional. Install it (winget/brew/apt as above), reopen the terminal, and confirm with gh --version.

stuck.problem: Push rejected: non-fast-forward / remote contains work you do not have.
stuck.fix: Someone (often your other machine) pushed first. Run git pull --rebase origin main, resolve any conflicts, then push again. Never force push to a shared branch.
